claims.statement: The fragment describes default commit-message newline cleanup and cleanup=verbatim for retaining the entered message. This source explanation is not a mandated cleanup setting or exhaustive Git configuration behavior; the linked Git reference remains separate and no imported command was executed.

A commit records branch file changes and has a hash identifying the commit, with change/time/creator metadata and a required brief descriptive message in the source explanation. Metadata is not cryptographically authenticated human identity, review approval or remote custody; committing is distinct from pushing and deployed state.

The pinned interaction-limit duration choices are 24 hours, 3 days, 1 week, 1 month and 6 months. These are source snapshot options, not a mandated default duration, current live availability or authorization to activate moderation.

Repository interaction limits restrict certain users from commenting, opening issues, creating PRs, emoji reactions, editing comments and editing issue/PR titles. The fragment does not define which users qualify or claim a complete read/write lock, Git-push block or permanent restriction. Audience applicability and effective behavior require additional context and native evidence; no limit changed.
